raccoon-removal.intro: St. Matthews is the Calhoun County seat — a small town of older homes and tree-lined streets in the farm country between Columbia and Orangeburg, where the housing stock is pre-war and postwar, the lots are generous, and most properties carry an outbuilding or two. Its raccoons are farm-country raccoons with town addresses: denning in the chimneys and attics of the older homes, living under the barns and well houses, and commuting the creek branches and fence lines that cross the town's edges. The spring pattern is the reliable one — a female in a chimney with kits, discovered by the chattering at dusk — and the fall pattern is the attic colony in a house that stood quiet over a working summer.
raccoon-removal.extendedBody:
Whole-parcel work in the county seat

A St. Matthews raccoon job surveys the parcel, not just the house, because the town's raccoons hold their territory across its structures: the chimney for the spring litter, the barn loft for the winter, the porch void for everything between. We remove the residents under the depredation permit for your property — chimney families taken together, on their timing — and seal the structures in sequence: flue caps, soffit and eave repairs in metal, crawlspace and loft openings screened, so the rotation ends for want of a next building. The ground gets its read as well: the fence-line runs and creek-bank routes that deliver the animals are named, and the feed and bin habits that hold a territory at your address are part of the conversation. In a town St. Matthews' size, the sealed farmstead is visible from the road by the absence of repeat visits, and that is the reference the work runs on.

faqs.q: How much does raccoon removal cost in St. Matthews?
faqs.a: It depends on how many structures the raccoons are using — a chimney family in the house alone is one job; a rotation across house, barn, and well house is a surveyed programme with sequenced sealing. We walk the whole parcel first and quote the complete job firmly before any trapping, with the structures ranked by activity. The depredation permit for your property is arranged as part of the work.

faqs.q: A raccoon has kits in our St. Matthews chimney. Can the family be taken together?
faqs.a: Yes — that is the standard we work to. A chimney litter is removed as a family: the mother and the kits together, handled so the young stay with her, and the flue is capped in the same programme so next spring's raccoon — quite possibly the same female, who remembers a proven chimney — finds it closed. What we will not do is trap the mother alone and leave the kits calling in the flue; if anyone proposes it, the crying you hear for the following nights is the reason it is not done that way.
